name: Eva Maria Braun-Luedicke
name_chinese: 伊娃·玛丽亚·布劳恩·卢迪克
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Eva Maria Braun-Luedicke owns 12% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
Her mother's cousin Ludwig Georg Braun took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
Eva Maria works as a Communications Manager for B. Braun.
forbes_facts: Eva Maria is a sixth-generation family member and her mother, Barbara, is a member of the company's supervisory board.
B. Braun has been operating in Africa for more than 60 years, and now has subsidiaries in Zambia, Algeria, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.

name: Thierry Cruanes
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2024); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
forbes_bio: Thierry Cruanes is a cofounder and the chief technology officer of Snowflake, a cloud-based database company.
Cruanes started Snowflake with fellow billoinaire Benoit Dageville and Marcin Zukowski in 2012.
Snowflake went public in 2020 and raised $3.9 billion, in what was then the largest software IPO in U.S. history.
Cruanes and Dageville met while working at Oracle.
forbes_facts: Cruanes has a Ph.D in computer science and holds more than 250 patents.

name: An Kang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2006-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2021)
forbes_bio: An Kang, a former doctor, is the chairman and largest shareholder of Hualan Biological Engineering, a producer of vaccines and blood products.
An won a national science award at age 29.
An's hobby includes reading.

name: Chung Mong-joon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Chung Mong-joon is the largest shareholder of shipbuilder HD Hyundai Heavy Industries.
He is the sixth son of the late Hyundai group founder Chung Ju-yung, who got his start repairing trucks for the U.S. Army after the Korean War.
Chung ran HD Hyundai Heavy Industries until he entered politics in 1988; he served seven terms in the National Assembly.
forbes_facts: In 2014, he ran for mayor of Seoul but lost.
He is a former vice president of international soccer body FIFA.

name: Henrietta Goh
forbes_bio: Henrietta Goh is a granddaughter of the late Singaporean paints tycoon Goh Cheng Liang, who died in August 2025 at age 98.
The Goh family draws the bulk of its wealth from a majority stake in Japan's Nippon Paint Holdings, one of the world's largest paint manufacturers.
Henrietta, together with her two sisters and three cousins, inherited the bulk of their grandfather's fortune.
Her father is Hup Jin, the eldest child of the late patriarch who started making paints in a small factory in Singapore before partnering with Nippon Paint in 1962.
Hup Jin is the chairman of Nippon Paint.

name: Thomas Bruch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Thomas Bruch's retail fortune derives from Globus, with roots dating back to 1828.
Globus operates hypermarkets and DIY stores in Germany, Luxembourg, Russia and Czech Republic. It employs almost 47,000 worldwide.
Bruch owns about 38% of the holding company; the rest is distributed among other family members, a family foundation and a charitable foundation.
The charitable Globus Stiftung -- of which Bruch's wife, Graciela, is CEO -- holds about 26% and will receive Bruch's stake after his death.
In 2020, his son Matthias took over as managing director of Globus, representing the sixth generation of the family to run the firm. He also holds 10% of the company.
forbes_facts: Globus Stiftung has supported more than 400 social projects with $10.5 million. It focuses on supporting youth in their transition from school to work.
Globus offers its 18,500 employees the chance to invest in and profit from the performance of the company though silent partnerships.

name: Hu Xingrong
appears_on: Hurun Global (2020-2025); Hurun China (2019-2024); Hurun Global U40 (2020-2021); Hurun China U40 (2019-2021)

name: Lu Lili
forbes_bio: Lu Lili derives her fortune from a minority stake in East Money Information and a 8.5% stake in Wanda Film Holding.
Lu is the wife of Qi Shi, who founded and chairs East Money Information, a provider of IT and software for the financial services industry in China.
She previously worked at the company's general manager's office.
Lu bought just over 8% of Wanda Film Holding for $306 million in 2023.

name: Tope Awotona
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Tope Awotona is the founder and CEO of scheduling software company Calendly.
Awotona, a former salesman for tech firms including EMC (now Dell EMC), founded Calendly out of his own frustration with the back-and-forth emails required to schedule meetings.
He bootstrapped Calendly for years before taking on a $350 million investment in 2021 that valued the firm at $3 billion.
Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Awotona immigrated to the United States as a teenager.
Before founding Calendly, he had started a few other businesses, including one that sold projectors and another that sold garden tools, that flopped.
forbes_facts: To build its first product, Awotona hired a Ukrainian firm for programming help and was in Kyiv during anti-government protests in 2014.

name: Elena Baturina
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Russia's second wealthiest woman, Elena Baturina, was married to Yury Luzkhkov, who was the mayor of Moscow for years.
In 2010, Luzhkov was removed from the mayor's post; Baturina and their daughters left the country.
Baturina soon sold almost all of her assets in Russia including a construction company called Inteko and a cement factories.
The Russian government seized land she owned in an exclusive area of Moscow. She filed a lawsuit, unsuccessfully demanding $1 billion in compensation.
Baturina, who now lives in London, owns real estate in Europe and USA, and invests in renewable energy.
forbes_facts: Baturina bought two commercial properties in Brooklyn near the Barclays Center in 2015.
Baturina's charity fund BE OPEN supports young designers, architects, writers and scientists.

name: Ilya Scherbovich
forbes_bio: Ilya Scherbovich established the investment manager UCP Investment Group in 2006.
Among his first deals were selling companies with exploration licences to Novatek and buying 10% of retail operator Fashion Continent.
UCP's assets under management currently exceed $3 billion.
Scherbovich has served on the boards of Russian state companies Sberbank, Transneft and Rosneft.

name: Lee Ho-jin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2025)
forbes_bio: Lee Ho-jin is a former chairman of Taekwang Industrial, a manufacturer that became synonymous with Korea's textile and petrochemical prowess.
He rose to chairman after his oldest brother, Lee Sik-jin, died. He has now stepped down and is reportedly struggling against liver cancer.
In 2011, he was sentenced to 54 months in prison for embezzling $128 million from the company but has been out on bail due to his illness.
In 2019, Lee was sentenced to three years in prison on charges of embezzlement and breach of trust. He was pardoned in 2023.
forbes_facts: Lee is credited for diversifying the group into media and entertainment.
His mother sold clothes in a Busan market and provided the seed money to start Taekwang, which began as a textile company.

name: Park Kwan-ho
forbes_bio: Park Kwan-ho is founder and chairman of WeMade, an online game developer, which he started in 2000.
Park took the company public on Korea's technology-rich Kosdaq stock exchange in 2009.
Previously, Park was the development team leader at Korean game developer ActozSoft.
